analysis: Conditional uncertainty for recoverable historical transfer predictions
scope: No training, no harmonization, no replacement of historical predictions by newly fitted models.
eligibility: A stored historical probability vector must be tied to the named direction and historical model source.
Patient/admission unit, original label, target patient grouping and denominator must be verified.
The directly recomputed AUC must reproduce the reported value at its original reporting precision.
A numerical match alone is not enough to certify an unrelated model as the historical source.

bootstrap.scheme: Ordinary non-stratified patient-cluster bootstrap; sample the original number of patients with replacement and retain all rows from each sampled patient with its sampling multiplicity.
bootstrap.statistic: AUROC using half credit for tied scores
bootstrap.interval: Two-sided percentile 95% interval, numpy linear quantiles at 0.025 and 0.975
bootstrap.degenerate_draws: Record and omit draws with only one outcome class; do not silently redraw.
bootstrap.conditioning: Fixed historical prediction vectors, fixed fitted source models and fixed historical preprocessing. No model-refitting, source-sampling, selection or mapping uncertainty is included.
bootstrap.patient_level_special_case: Each recovered Chinese target has one row per patient, so the patient-cluster bootstrap reduces to patient resampling.

verification: Compare original and manuscript-copy historical probabilities and labels by centre and patient key without outputting keys.
Compare Chinese labels with the original patient_level_data.csv label source.
Check weighted tie-aware AUROC against sklearn and explicit row replication, including unequal cluster multiplicities.
Repeat the deterministic bootstrap in a separate verify invocation and compare all replicate values and summary intervals.
Record source, protocol, code and output hashes plus the runtime versions.
limitations: These intervals do not establish prospective prediction, absence of temporal leakage, clinical utility or a common cross-centre task.
No CI may be inferred from aggregate AUC values alone.
Unrecovered directions remain unavailable, with a bounded search record and explicit recovery requirements.
